 ADVERTISEMENT   Filtered By: Sports Sports Joshua Pacio out to break 'Japan curse' at ONE SAMURAI 5 
 By RAFAEL BANDAYREL Published November 17, 2026 3:43pm 
 + Add GMA on Google Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google. Photo: ONE Championship Joshua Pacio is looking to settle unfinished business in Japan when he puts his ONE Strawweight MMA World Championship on the line against Japanese challenger Keito Yamakita on Wednesday, November 18.
 The Filipino champion headlines ONE SAMURAI 5 at the EBARA WAVE Arena Ota in Tokyo, where he hopes to overcome his previous setback in the country and retain his undisputed crown.
 Pacio, who represents Lions Nation MMA, admitted that returning to Japan carries extra motivation after losing on his previous visit. When he last fought in the country, Pacio fell short in his quest to gain double-champion status against Yuya Wakamatsu in November 2025.
 “I am very happy to be able to come to Japan to compete in ONE SAMURAI 5 like this,” Pacio said. “I am grateful for this opportunity. I have prepared thoroughly for this event, and I am completely ready.”

 “The last time that I was here, I lost. Right now, I’d like to prove that I can win here. People say that there’s a Japan curse. We can’t win here. On Wednesday night, it’s going to be ‘And still.’”
 Standing in his way is Yamakita, a Japanese submission specialist who enters the championship bout with an undefeated record in ONE Championship and a formidable grappling game.
 Pacio acknowledged the threat posed by the hometown hero, but believes his improvements on the ground will help him neutralize Yamakita's submission game.
 “[Yamakita] is a worthy opponent and a worthy challenger. I can see his hunger to get the belt. His caliber as an athlete is not something to take lightly.”
 —JMB, GMA News
